topics.titleEn: Cut Your Observability Bill: Sampling and Cardinality
topics.angle: how-to|Slash logging and metrics spend without going blind, using sampling and cardinality control.
topics.brief: Sections: why observability bills explode (high-cardinality labels, debug logs, retained raw traces); tactics (tail-based trace sampling, log levels and drop rules, metric cardinality limits, tiered retention, moving to OTel Collector pipelines); what you can safely cut vs must keep for incidents; measuring the savings. Verify: tail-based sampling and cardinality cost drivers in 2026; OTel Collector processors. Sources: OpenTelemetry docs; observability-cost writeups. Distinct from 'Observability 101' and 'FinOps': focused on cutting telemetry cost.

topics.titleTr: Her PR için Dallanan Önizleme Veritabanları
topics.titleEn: Branching Preview Databases for Every PR
topics.angle: how-to|Give every pull request a real, isolated database using copy-on-write branching.
topics.brief: Sections: why shared staging DBs break preview envs; copy-on-write DB branching (Neon-style) and when to use snapshots/containers instead; wiring a branch-per-PR into CI with seed/anonymized data; cost and teardown; migration testing on a branch before merge. Verify: DB branching/copy-on-write approaches and data-masking in 2026; teardown automation. Sources: Neon/Postgres branching docs; preview-env writeups. Distinct from 'Preview Environments for Every PR' (app envs) and 'Database Backups': focused on per-PR database branching.

topics.titleTr: AI İş Yükleri için GPU Maliyetini Kontrol Et
topics.titleEn: Cut GPU Costs for AI Workloads: Spot and Scheduling
topics.angle: how-to|Cut GPU spend for inference and training with spot, bin-packing and right-sizing.
topics.brief: Sections: why GPU bills dominate AI infra; tactics (spot/preemptible with checkpointing, MIG/fractional GPUs, bin-packing and autoscaling to zero, batching and quantization, right-sizing model to hardware); queueing and scheduling for bursty jobs; measuring $/token and utilization. Verify: spot-GPU savings and interruption handling; MIG/fractional GPU and scale-to-zero in 2026. Sources: cloud GPU pricing docs; MLOps cost writeups. Distinct from 'Kubernetes Cost Optimization' and 'FinOps': GPU/AI-workload specific.

topics.titleTr: Gemini Canvas ile Ham Veriden Canlı Panel
topics.titleEn: Build a Live Dashboard From Raw Data in Gemini
topics.angle: how-to|Turn messy raw data into an interactive dashboard with Gemini 3's Canvas.
topics.brief: Sections: what Canvas does (generate enterprise-quality interactive dashboards from unintuitive data); a walkthrough (upload raw data, prompt for tabs/sortable tables/trend views, refine); exporting or sharing; accuracy checks on AI-inferred metrics; when a real BI tool is still better. Verify: Gemini 3 Canvas dashboard capability and tiers (2026); export/share options. Sources: blog.google Gemini 3 examples; Gemini release notes. Distinct from 'Claude Artifacts pull live data via MCP': a Gemini Canvas how-to for non-analysts.

topics.titleTr: Akıl Yürütme Ayarı: Ne Zaman Derin Düşün?
topics.titleEn: Tune Reasoning Effort in Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini
topics.angle: how-to|Use the new reasoning-effort controls to get better answers without burning tokens.
topics.brief: Sections: why 'think harder' isn't free (reasoning burns tokens/time/cost); the controls in 2026 (ChatGPT's reasoning-effort slider replacing Instant/Thinking; Gemini Deep Think levels; Claude extended thinking); a decision guide by task (quick lookup vs multi-step analysis vs coding); cost/latency tradeoffs and defaults. Verify: ChatGPT reasoning-effort slider (Aug/Sept 2026); Gemini Deep Think levels; Claude thinking controls. Sources: OpenAI/Gemini release notes; Claude docs. Distinct from the ChatGPT 'Thinking slider' news post: a cross-tool how-to on tuning effort and cost.

topics.titleEn: How to Fact-Check Your AI Assistant: A Checklist
topics.angle: checklist|A practical checklist for everyday users to catch AI hallucinations before they bite.
topics.brief: Sections: where assistants reliably make things up (citations, numbers, quotes, code APIs, legal/medical); the checklist (demand sources and open them, cross-check across tools, ask for uncertainty, verify quotes/figures at the primary source, beware confident specifics); prompts that reduce fabrication; tools with live search vs memory. Verify: hallucination patterns and citation-fabrication rates in 2026; grounding/search effects. Sources: model-eval and safety writeups; provider help docs. A consumer checklist distinct from the production 'reduce hallucinations' engineering post.
